hints.title: Find the rounding units
hints.body: Identify the place value of the last retained significant figure for the area. For each measurement, subtract and add half of its rounding unit.
hints.recap: Each rounding instruction defines its own interval.
hints.pitfall: Two significant figures and nearest centimetre use different units of uncertainty.
hints.pause: Write both measurement intervals, keeping track of excluded upper endpoints.

recall.reminder: Use half the rounding unit to form the measurement bounds.

hints.title: Choose endpoints after rearranging
hints.body: Express height as area divided by width. For positive quantities, ask how increasing the numerator or denominator changes a quotient.
hints.recap: An upper bound on a quotient uses favourable endpoints from both intervals.
hints.pitfall: An excluded endpoint gives a limiting bound, not necessarily an attained maximum.
hints.pause: Select the appropriate two endpoints and keep their quotient exact.

recall.reminder: Optimise only over the permitted measurement ranges.

solution:
The measurement ranges are 5550≤A<5650 and 79.5≤w<80.5. Since h=A/w, its limiting upper bound is 565079.5 cm. Answer F.

The upper area endpoint is not attained under the usual rounding convention; the expression in the options is the upper bound approached by possible heights.
